title.narrative: WGG- Research and Documentation in Kenya

description.narrative: The strategy of research and documentation is integral to the learning and evidence building agenda of the WGG Consortium and its country-level strategic partners. There are significant programmatic components of the consortium wide joint activities as part of global and regional advocacy efforts.

sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

Trainings on feminist, leadership skills and Movement building for 30 Young Women and Girls, Women Rights Organizations, Women Rights Networks alliances in Mombasa County, engagement in feminist leadership institute and leadership academy for girls

(i) Young women’s engagement in sports advocacy reached 900 youth, building knowledge and skills to address violence in sports and institutions like Technical and Vocational Education and Trainings ( TVETs). (ii) Trained 22 diverse women community leaders (18 women, 4 PWDs with their caregivers) and 4 men to become paralegals on handling SGBV case management and the legal approach to access to justice in the six Sub-Counties in Mombasa County. (iii) Trained 27 Chama women on traits of an abuser and that of a victim, forms of SGBV, steps to take to support a GBV survivor, referral pathway, technology-facilitated GBV, process of access to justice, legal frameworks for addressing SGBV cases, and support systems at the community level. (iv) Engaged 37 (2PWDs and their caregivers, 34 YW) diverse teenage girls and caregivers to the children living with disability on Femme Tribe conversations which covered sexual exploitation, sexual harassment, sex trafficking and sexual grooming in Mombasa County.

In Mombasa we had 13 journalists and Nyanza had 8 journalists. FGDs with strategic partners to inform the development of an SGBV Curriculum

Akili Dada held focus group discussions with 28 young women including WWG in Kenya. The focus of the conversations was to explore the young women’s perspective on SGBV and also inform the development of an SGBV curriculum.
